steps.title: Agent Registry console page
steps.what: The documented flow is a four-step Add Agent wizard in the Agent Registry.
steps.why: Agents that call models, tool servers and other agents need to be first-class identities with an owner, an expiry, a lifecycle and per-agent policy, not anonymous API keys.

steps.title: Add Agent and Edit Agent wizard
steps.what: The documented flow is a four-step Add Agent wizard in the Agent Registry.
steps.why: Agents that call models, tool servers and other agents need to be first-class identities with an owner, an expiry, a lifecycle and per-agent policy, not anonymous API keys.

steps.title: Custodian
steps.what: (1) Identity and Access sets the agent name (permanent; renaming means delete and recreate), custodian, expiry and scopes (llm, mcp, a2a).
steps.why: Agents that call models, tool servers and other agents need to be first-class identities with an owner, an expiry, a lifecycle and per-agent policy, not anonymous API keys.

steps.title: Agent access key
steps.what: (1) Identity and Access sets the agent name (permanent; renaming means delete and recreate), custodian, expiry and scopes (llm, mcp, a2a).
steps.why: Agents that call models, tool servers and other agents need to be first-class identities with an owner, an expiry, a lifecycle and per-agent policy, not anonymous API keys.

steps.title: Grant policy created when apps are selected
steps.what: For mcp or a2a, it sets the specific apps (and optionally specific MCP tools) the agent may reach; selecting them is the grant, and saving creates a grant policy for the custodian tied to the key.
steps.why: Agents that call models, tool servers and other agents need to be first-class identities with an owner, an expiry, a lifecycle and per-agent policy, not anonymous API keys.

steps.title: Per-key Runtime Protection
steps.what: (3) Runtime Protection sets the AI Guard configuration for that key; AI Guard is configured per agent key, not per app.
steps.why: Agents that call models, tool servers and other agents need to be first-class identities with an owner, an expiry, a lifecycle and per-agent policy, not anonymous API keys.

steps.title: Federated Identity object
steps.what: The documentation also describes a second custodian option, a secretless Federated Identity (the former Non-Human Identity; the API object is still NonHumanIdentity) with federation settings (issuer, audience, subject, key set location, maximum token lifetime, required claims).
steps.why: Agents that call models, tool servers and other agents need to be first-class identities with an owner, an expiry, a lifecycle and per-agent policy, not anonymous API keys.

steps.title: Privilege gateway
steps.what: (2) Gateway and Apps sets, for llm, one provider per key, allowed models, requests per minute, tokens per minute and a budget; the real provider key is stored in Privilege and injected server-side, so LLM-scoped keys are created here and need the real provider key in hand.
steps.why: Agents that call models, tool servers and other agents need to be first-class identities with an owner, an expiry, a lifecycle and per-agent policy, not anonymous API keys.
